# Trigger.dev v4.8.7

> Documentation generated from the latest stable release of [triggerdotdev/trigger.dev](https://github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev) and pinned to immutable source commit `fae01445473658369323ddc462b71eae51c790ff`.

- [Full documentation](llms-full.txt): Complete normalized corpus for Trigger.dev v4.8.7.
- [Provenance manifest](manifest.json): Release, commit, document count, and generation notes.
- Pages follow the navigation declared in docs/docs.json at the immutable release tag; snippets are inlined into the pages that import them rather than published separately.
- API reference pages are rendered from the OpenAPI specification the page names in its `openapi` frontmatter, since the upstream page carries no prose of its own.
- Static MDX cards, tabs, accordions, steps, callouts, and parameter fields are normalized to Markdown without executing JavaScript.
- Published page links resolve to https://trigger.dev/docs; source assets point at the immutable release commit.
- Quarantined sources (3): upstream pages using constructs this generator cannot convert yet are omitted and listed in `manifest.json`.

## Getting started

- [Trigger.dev docs](pages/introduction.md): Build and run durable AI agents and workflows in TypeScript. Long-running tasks with retries, queues, webhooks, observability, and elastic scaling. Open source and self-hostable. (10010 bytes)
- [Quick start: add Trigger.dev to your project](pages/quick-start.md): Set up Trigger.dev in your existing project in under 3 minutes. Install the SDK, create your first background task, and trigger it from your code. (5092 bytes)

- [Limits](pages/limits.md): There are some hard and soft limits that you might hit. (15982 bytes)

## Fundamentals

- [Connect to AWS](pages/oidc/aws.md): Assume an IAM role from your tasks without storing AWS access keys. (8927 bytes)
- [Connect to Microsoft Azure](pages/oidc/azure.md): Authenticate to Azure from your tasks with a federated identity credential instead of a client secret or certificate. (4233 bytes)

- [Connect to Anthropic](pages/oidc/anthropic.md): Call Claude from your tasks and chat agents without storing an Anthropic API key. (8963 bytes)
- [Connect to HashiCorp Vault](pages/oidc/vault.md): Log in to Vault from your tasks with JWT auth instead of a long-lived Vault token. (2964 bytes)
- [Connect to Infisical](pages/oidc/infisical.md): Read secrets from Infisical using your task's workload identity. (3244 bytes)
- [Connect to Doppler](pages/oidc/doppler.md): Fetch secrets from Doppler in your tasks with a service account identity instead of a stored Doppler token. (3142 bytes)
- [Connect to Snowflake](pages/oidc/snowflake.md): Connect to Snowflake from your tasks with workload identity federation instead of a password or private key. (3466 bytes)
- [Connect to Databricks](pages/oidc/databricks.md): Authenticate to Databricks from your tasks with a federation policy instead of a personal access token or client secret. (3944 bytes)
- [Connect to Hugging Face](pages/oidc/hugging-face.md): Exchange a Trigger.dev OIDC token for a short-lived Hugging Face token to run inference, download gated models or read one repo, without storing an HF\TOKEN. (5214 bytes)
- [Connect to OpenRouter](pages/oidc/openrouter.md): Exchange a Trigger.dev OIDC token for a short-lived OpenRouter access token, so your tasks call models without an OPENROUTER\API\KEY. (4225 bytes)

## Agents

- [AI Agents](pages/ai-chat/overview.md): Durable multi-turn AI chats — one Trigger.dev task per conversation, surviving refreshes, deploys, and crashes. (5368 bytes)
- [Quick Start](pages/ai-chat/quick-start.md): Define an agent, authorize chat sessions on your server, and stream responses into a React frontend. (7057 bytes)
- [Migrate from an AI SDK route handler](pages/ai-chat/migrating-from-a-route-handler.md): Move an existing useChat + streamText chat app to chat.agent — what stays identical, what you delete, and a prompt you can hand to a coding agent. (33833 bytes)
- [Anatomy of an agent](pages/ai-chat/anatomy.md): The three parts of a chat agent — the agent task that runs the turn loop, the durable session that carries messages, and the frontend transport — what each does and where it's documented. (4793 bytes)
- [Backend](pages/ai-chat/backend.md): Three approaches to building your chat backend — chat.agent(), session iterator, or raw task primitives. (45397 bytes)
- [Lifecycle hooks](pages/ai-chat/lifecycle-hooks.md): Hook into every stage of a chat agent's run: preload, turn start, turn complete, suspend, resume, and more. (42848 bytes)
- [Tools](pages/ai-chat/tools.md): Declare tools on chat.agent so toModelOutput survives across turns, get them back typed in run(), and type your messages from them. (11086 bytes)
- [Frontend](pages/ai-chat/frontend.md): Transport setup, session management, client data, and frontend patterns for AI Chat. (31210 bytes)
- [Server-Side Chat](pages/ai-chat/server-chat.md): Use AgentChat to interact with chat agents from server-side code — tasks, webhooks, scripts, or other agents. (13646 bytes)
- [Sessions](pages/ai-chat/sessions.md): A Session is a stateful execution of an agent, with two-way streaming and durable compute. A single Session can have multiple runs associated with it. (20363 bytes)
- [Side channels](pages/ai-chat/side-channels.md): Named, durable stream pairs on a Session, separate from the chat transcript. A side channel outlives a single run, is shared across runs, and its input does not wake a run. (8627 bytes)
- [chat.local](pages/ai-chat/chat-local.md): Typed, run-scoped data accessible from hooks, run(), tools, and subtasks. Survives across turns, auto-cleared between runs, auto-hydrated into subtasks. (6811 bytes)
- [Types](pages/ai-chat/types.md): TypeScript types for AI Agents, UI messages, and the frontend transport. (10292 bytes)
- [Custom agents](pages/ai-chat/custom-agents.md): Build chat agents without chat.agent()'s managed lifecycle: register with chat.customAgent(), then drive turns with the createSession iterator or a hand-rolled loop. (34338 bytes)
- [How the AI Agents SDK works](pages/ai-chat/how-it-works.md): End-to-end mechanics of a chat.agent turn: the two durable channels per session, the long-lived task that reads and writes them, and how a chat survives refreshes, deploys, and idle gaps. (20773 bytes)
- [Prompts](pages/ai/prompts.md): Define prompt templates as code, version them on deploy, and override from the dashboard without redeploying. (14566 bytes)
- [LLM observability](pages/ai/observability.md): Capture Vercel AI SDK calls in a task as spans in the run trace, with model, token usage, cost, and latency. Link calls to prompt versions and query usage across runs. (7732 bytes)
- [Fast starts](pages/ai-chat/fast-starts.md): Two ways to cut first-turn TTFC: Preload eagerly triggers the run before the first message; Head Start runs step 1 in your warm server while the agent boots in parallel. (39654 bytes)
- [Compaction](pages/ai-chat/compaction.md): Automatic context compaction to keep long conversations within token limits. (16931 bytes)
- [Prompt caching](pages/ai-chat/prompt-caching.md): Cache the stable prefix of your agent's prompt with Anthropic prompt caching to cut token cost and latency on every turn. (12420 bytes)
- [Pending Messages](pages/ai-chat/pending-messages.md): Inject user messages mid-execution to steer agents between tool-call steps. (16675 bytes)
- [Background injection](pages/ai-chat/background-injection.md): Inject context from background work into the agent's conversation: self-review, RAG augmentation, or any async analysis. (16611 bytes)
- [Actions](pages/ai-chat/actions.md): Custom commands sent from the frontend that mutate chat state without consuming a turn: undo, rollback, edit, regenerate. (8295 bytes)
- [Transcript storage](pages/ai-chat/transcript-storage.md): Where a chat.agent conversation is kept: the UIMessages the runtime saves, the platform default, reading history back, and bringing your own database through the TranscriptStorage adapter. (18923 bytes)
- [Migrate from hydrateMessages to transcript storage](pages/ai-chat/migrating-from-hydrate-messages.md): Move a chat.agent that persists its own history through hydrateMessages onto a TranscriptStorage: map your tables, implement load and save, decide whether you need loadContext, and delete the recovery and compaction cod… (17134 bytes)
- [Error handling](pages/ai-chat/error-handling.md): How errors flow through chat.agent — stream errors, hook errors, run failures — and how to recover. (16657 bytes)
- [Channels (chat frontends)](pages/webhooks/channels.md): Point Slack (or any chat surface) at an agent: messages become turns and replies post back. (12066 bytes)
- [Slack agents](pages/webhooks/slack.md): Turn a chat.agent into a Slack agent: users message it in Slack, it shows its status while it works, streams its reply with its tool calls as a plan, asks for approvals, and stops on Slack's stop button. (28027 bytes)
- [Linear agents](pages/webhooks/linear.md): Turn a chat.agent into a Linear agent: assign it an issue or @mention it, and it works the issue inside Linear's agent session UI. (18790 bytes)

- [Sub-Agents](pages/ai-chat/patterns/sub-agents.md): Delegate work to durable sub-agents from a parent agent's tool calls, and stream each sub-agent's work to the frontend as it happens. (19912 bytes)
- [Version upgrades](pages/ai-chat/patterns/version-upgrades.md): Gracefully migrate chat agents to a new deployment using chat.requestUpgrade(), chat.endAndContinue(), and the continuation mechanism. (13246 bytes)
- [Database persistence for chat](pages/ai-chat/patterns/database-persistence.md): Split conversation state and live session metadata across hooks — preload, turn start, turn complete — without tying the pattern to a specific ORM or schema. (20592 bytes)
- [Persistence and replay](pages/ai-chat/patterns/persistence-and-replay.md): How chat.agent rebuilds conversation history at run boot — the transcript storage's persisted conversation plus session.out replay, and what changes when your app owns the model's context. (15518 bytes)
- [Branching conversations](pages/ai-chat/patterns/branching-conversations.md): Persist an active conversation branch and use transcript storage and actions to switch the agent's context. (7731 bytes)
- [Code execution sandbox](pages/ai-chat/patterns/code-sandbox.md): Warm an isolated sandbox on each chat turn, run an AI SDK executeCode tool, and tear down right before the run suspends — using chat.agent hooks and chat.local. (5339 bytes)

- [Tool result auditing](pages/ai-chat/patterns/tool-result-auditing.md): Find new tool results before they merge into chat history, and deduplicate audit writes with a durable idempotency key. (7117 bytes)
- [Large payloads in chat.agent](pages/ai-chat/patterns/large-payloads.md): Why a single chunk on the chat stream is capped at \1 MiB, what error you'll see, and how to work around it with ID references. (6613 bytes)
- [Agent Skills](pages/ai-chat/patterns/skills.md): Ship reusable capabilities (folders with SKILL.md + scripts) that a chat agent discovers and invokes on demand. (10098 bytes)
- [OOM resilience](pages/ai-chat/patterns/oom-resilience.md): Recover from out-of-memory errors mid-turn by automatically retrying the failed turn on a larger machine — without losing the in-flight user message or re-processing completed turns. (7043 bytes)
- [Recovery boot](pages/ai-chat/patterns/recovery-boot.md): Recover from cancel-mid-stream, crashes, and OOM kills with full conversational context. The smart default Just Works; the onRecoveryBoot hook is the override path for advanced policies. (11689 bytes)
- [Trusted edge signals](pages/ai-chat/patterns/trusted-edge-signals.md): How to safely deliver server-trusted signals (bot scores, JA4, ASN, ReCAPTCHA verdicts) to a chat.agent run via an edge proxy. (15855 bytes)
- [Redact chat content from traces](pages/ai-chat/patterns/redacting-telemetry.md): Stop a chat agent recording user messages and clientData on its spans, turn off AI SDK prompt and response recording, or redact span content with a span processor before it leaves the worker. (7649 bytes)
- [Native compaction & provider fallback](pages/ai-chat/patterns/native-compaction.md): Persist provider-native compaction (Anthropic context editing, OpenAI stored responses) across chat.agent turns so history is never re-sent, and fall back between providers without losing the conversation. (16944 bytes)

- [Client Protocol](pages/ai-chat/client-protocol.md): The wire protocol for building custom chat transports — how clients communicate with chat agents over Sessions and SSE. (78438 bytes)
- [Testing](pages/ai-chat/testing.md): Drive a chat.agent through real turns in unit tests — no network, no task runtime, no mocking the SDK. (34018 bytes)

- [Supabase webhooks](pages/webhooks/providers/supabase.md): Receive Supabase database webhooks with Trigger.dev. Check a shared bearer secret and run a task for each insert, update or delete. (2178 bytes)
- [Tailscale webhooks](pages/webhooks/providers/tailscale.md): Receive and verify Tailscale webhooks with Trigger.dev. Check the HMAC-SHA256 signature in tailscale-webhook-signature and run a task for each Tailscale event. (2272 bytes)
- [Typeform webhooks](pages/webhooks/providers/typeform.md): Receive and verify Typeform webhooks with Trigger.dev. Check the HMAC-SHA256 signature in typeform-signature and run a task for each Typeform event, filtered on event.event\type. (2301 bytes)
- [Vapi webhooks](pages/webhooks/providers/vapi.md): Receive and verify Vapi webhooks with Trigger.dev. Check the HMAC-SHA256 signature in x-vapi-signature and run a task for each Vapi event, filtered on event.message.type. (2442 bytes)
- [Vercel webhooks](pages/webhooks/providers/vercel.md): Receive and verify Vercel webhooks with Trigger.dev. Check the HMAC-SHA1 signature in x-vercel-signature and run a task for each Vercel event, filtered on event.type. (1975 bytes)

- [Custom webhook providers](pages/webhooks/custom-providers.md): Verify webhooks from a provider that isn't built in by passing your own HMAC, shared-secret, URL-secret or public-key configuration to webhooks.custom(). (5283 bytes)
